text:
alex: Heads up — seeing steady VRAM growth in the KV cache for long chat sessions. Repro on both H100 and MI250 nightly runners. Looks like pages are being allocated but not reclaimed.

maria: Can you paste the repro steps and a quick profiler dump?

alex: Repro steps: 
```
./run_infer --model paged-attn-24b --seq 32768 --clients 8 --iters 10000 --kv-mode=paged --trace-kv=allocs
```
Short run shows monotonic vram +11GB over 10k tokens on H100 and +14GB on MI250.

cheng: Do you have the KV counters? evict_count / free_count / hoarded_spans etc.

alex: Quick counters from the trace: 
```
evicted_pages: 0
free_pages: 42
allocated_pages: 1700
hoarded_spans: 128
pt_fragmentation_pct: 37
last_free_epoch: 0
```
Spikes in hoarded_spans right after large batched requests.

sasha: Interesting — on H100 we see periodic PT retire events, on MI250 the retire callbacks appear never to run. Could be a DMA/unmap ordering mismatch or different alignment behaviour in the kernels.

junaid: Runtime note: compaction path uses an atomic slotmap CAS and then signals a background sweeper. If the CAS loses and the signal gets dropped we can end up with hoarded spans that never reach the free list. I suspect a lost wakeup race under heavy batching.

alex: I tried a local quick patch that adds an explicit memory_fence + guaranteed wakeup to the sweeper (branch fix/kv-compact-fence). Microbench: before patch = ~11GB drift after 10k tokens, after patch = ~2GB. Not stable across archs yet.

maria: Nice. Can you add the exact profiler snippet so we can add a CI guard?

alex: Snippet I used: 
```
# trace kv allocs every 1s and dump counters
trace_kv_enable(); sleep 60; trace_kv_dump("/tmp/kvtrace.json");
```
Also 1-line kernel selector log showed we run 256-byte-aligned tiled kernels on H100, 512-byte on MI250 for the same model config — might affect page coalescing.

sasha: If alignment differs we can create non-uniform span sizing and cause fragmentation. On MI the slab allocator expects 512 alignment for efficient coalescing; misaligned returns will produce many small fragments.

junaid: Agreed — two orthogonal bugs: (1) lost-wakeup in compaction signalling (fix in branch), (2) alignment mismatch from kernel selection leading to fragment non-coalescing. We should treat both.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout started for build 2026.03.18-kv-fix-1 to 10% of infer-nodes. :rocket:

cheng: I'll run the canary across an H100 and MI250 node farm tomorrow and collect kvtrace + dmesg. Will also run the microbench harness with varying batch sizes to hit the race.

alex: Notes for repro flakiness: larger batches + mixed kernel selection (autokernel that picks different tiling) increases hoard probability. Reproducer flags: `--autokernel=on --batch-size=64 --pinned-workers=4`.

maria: Can we add an e2e job that runs for 2M tokens across both archs and fails on >5GB leak?

junaid: I'll add unit tests for the CAS->signal path and a small kernel selector assertion ensuring alignment consistency per model variant.

sasha: I'll audit the dma_unmap and page-retire ordering on MI250 driver shim, seems suspicious.

alex: Thanks all — action items: cheng run canary + collect traces, sasha audit DMA/unmap order, junaid add tests, maria add CI guard. I'll push the fence patch and a follow-up alignment diagnostic to the branch.

maria: :thumbsup: keep updates here and paste the canary logs.
